audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Talon all seven rows, the content layer gave Brand all seven, and the packet itself flags that a Brand 7/7 chart cannot sit next to a 47.96% win rate.
audit.why: Brand genuinely owns levels 1-2: Talon's longest lane tool is Rake at 650 and his leap is 575, against Pillar of Flame at 900 and Sear at 1050, with no sustain. From level 3 the picture inverts — W into Q with three Wound stacks is a real kill combo on an immobile mage who has exactly one stun, and Assassin's Path costs him no ability cooldown to pick the angle. Late, Brand's AoE and the fact that Talon must walk through his zone to reach a backline hand the last row back.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Brand, Brand, Talon, Talon, Talon, Talon, Brand across both layers, with every why and whys rewritten to argue for the side its row now names.
sources: enemyKit Q 575 leap, W 650, E no cooldown, R 100/80/60

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and the mid text call his ultimate 'Rake'.
audit.why: Rake is his W. The ultimate is Shadow Assault, 100/80/60s, 550 range, which grants invisibility, bonus move speed and a converging blade ring on reappearance. That is the level-6 spike and the reason his all-in stops needing to start from your stun range.
audit.corrected: Named Shadow Assault with its 100s rank-1 cooldown and described what it actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says his engage is a 'W-vault' and that Pillar of Flame stuns.
audit.why: W (Rake) is a ranged dagger volley at 650 that damages on the way out and again on the return with a slow; it is not a dash. His gap-closers are Noxian Diplomacy (Q), which leaps when the target is outside melee range, at 575 and 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, and Assassin's Path (E), which vaults terrain with no meaningful ability cooldown — only the used wall goes on cooldown. On Brand's side, Pillar of Flame does no CC at all: only Sear (Q) stuns, and only against a target already ablaze, so Conflagration (E, 625, 13s at rank 1) must land first. Blaze also keeps ticking after he leaves with Shadow Assault, which the page already gets right.
audit.corrected: Engage renamed to the Q leap and the E wall vault; the stun corrected to the ablaze-gated Sear.

audit.why: The field exists to carry the numbers a player counts against.
audit.corrected: Rake 9s, the Q leap 8s, Assassin's Path free of its own cooldown, Shadow Assault 100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do's/Don'ts bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Titles promised ward discipline and W-greed; the bodies described the trade combo.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles using Assassin's Path and the 8s Q leap.

edits.before: Talon has no way to trade with you at range — his entire kit revolves around vaulting in with W and landing a full combo, which your faster Pillar stun punishes hard if he ever commits. Play a bit cautious near walls where his vault range extends, but otherwise you can freely poke him down on approach since he has nothing to answer with from a distance. This is a lane where patience and stun timing win almost every exchange.
edits.after: Talon has no way to trade with you at range — his kit revolves around the Noxian Diplomacy leap at 575 and Rake's returning daggers, and only an ablaze target can be stunned, so E has to land before Q. Play cautious near walls, where Assassin's Path hands him a free angle for nothing, but otherwise poke him down on approach since he has no answer from a distance. Patience and stun timing win the first two levels.

edits.before: The same pattern holds through level 6 — his Rake ultimate adds mobility and reset potential but doesn't change the fact that he has to close distance into your stun range first, so keep punishing any engage attempt. If he goes for a roam instead of a lane all-in, that's often the safer play for him since his combo simply doesn't win the direct trade against your poke and CC.
edits.after: Level 6 flips the lane — Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1, hides him and resets his position, so he no longer has to walk into your stun to open. Hold the wave short, ward the walls Assassin's Path vaults, and step up only while Rake is on its 9-second cooldown. If he leaves to roam, shove and track him on the minimap instead of chasing, and arrive with the stun already banked.

notes: This is the one matchup in the slice where I moved the verdict rather than just reconciling layers. The packet's own defect list flags that a Brand 7/7 chart cannot coexist with a 47.96% win rate, the full layer already said Talon on all seven rows, and the full-layer prose (HARD, 8/10, 'flammable AND immobile') has always argued Talon. I set both layers to Brand, Brand, Talon, Talon, Talon, Talon, Brand and rewrote every why and whys on a moved row so the sentence matches its verdict. Confidence is Medium on the exact row boundaries and High on the direction. Ratings left untouched — in this data the rating reads as stage intensity rather than ownership. suspectNames flagged wants.foe[2] 'Use Shadow Assault': that is Talon's real ultimate name and a false positive.
